newsitem.title: USA: Intraday CSCE world sugar lower as specs sell.
newsitem.headline: Intraday CSCE world sugar lower as specs sell.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures were weaker but up from morning lows by midsession as trade buying stymied further losses, traders said.
Early speculative selling in July pressured the spot month to a low of 11.26 cents a lb. Trade buying in the spreads halted losses and lifted prices slightly off the lows, dealers said.
"We are seeing the trade continue to be a steady buyer of spreads, while the spec selling has backed off," a floor source said.
Trade shortcovering in the October and March contracts was also noted, but producer scale-up selling is likely to limit gains at the day's highs.

The speculators still hold a heavy net long position in July with just nine trading days before the contract expires on June 30. As of early Monday, open interest stood at 58,088 lots, donw 4,245 lots from the previous session.
At 1125 EDT, July was 0.07 cent lower at 11.29 cents, with most-active October down 0.06 cent at 11.22 cents and the outer months 0.04 higher to 0.02 lower.
The July/October spread narrowed to 0.07 cent from 0.08 cent on Monday's close.
Volume was estimated at 16,102 lots as of 1100 EDT.
